newsitem.title: FRANCE: French surgeons accused of unnecessary operations.
newsitem.headline: French surgeons accused of unnecessary operations.

text.p: Two French surgeons went on trial on Wednesday accused of carrying out unnecessary surgery on patients believed to be ill with prostate cancer.
Urologists Pierre Leandri and Georges Rossignol face up to 10 years in prison if they are convicted of wilfully causing bodily harm causing mutilation or permanent disability.
The prosecution, out of complaints from 43 patients, says surgery in 18 cases of bladder removal may not have been necessary.
The surgeons, who sometimes operated together and had an international reputation say that, if mistakes were made, they were involuntary errors of diagnosis.
Experts told the court in the southwestern town of Toulouse that in at least six cases a hasty decision was made on surgery at the expense of other treatments.

Presiding judge Jean Boyer said the surgeons, in order to buy shares in the private clinic where they worked, had commited themselves to a minimum turnover. "You had two possibilities: have more patients or more surgery on each patient," he said.
